articles.title: Banana producers in Latin America want better pay to cope with effects of climate crisis
articles.highlight: 拉丁美洲香蕉生产者呼吁提高报酬，以应对气候危机，因为今年超级厄尔尼诺引发的极端天气正导致产量大幅下降。
articles.summary: 文章称，拉丁美洲香蕉生产者正面临超级厄尔尼诺带来的极端天气，产量已明显下降。哥伦比亚的大风、秘鲁和厄瓜多尔的强降雨，以及多米尼加共和国预计的干旱，都在影响生产。生产商因此呼吁改善报酬，以增强应对气候危机的能力。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键点在于，气候风险会沿供应链传导为生产波动和农民收入压力，公平贸易与价格机制是缓冲手段之一。
articles.sourceExcerpt: Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event. High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body. In the Dominican Republic, farmers are expected to face drought conditions, with forecasts of drier and warmer than usual conditions.

articles.title: Hope Is the Thing with Feathers, and with Fangs: The Alchemy of Unrequited Love and the Story Behind Emily Dickinson’s Most Famous Poem
articles.highlight: 自九月以来，我怀有一种恐惧——无人可诉，于是我歌唱，就像男孩在墓地旁那样——因为我害怕。
articles.summary: 这篇随笔改编自《Figuring》第十九章，从狄金森三十岁初秋写给希金森的信中“无人可诉的恐惧”入手，追索她最著名诗作《希望是长着羽毛的东西》背后的情感经验。传记作者多年来用死亡等猜测填补这段空白，文章则关注她如何把恐惧与单恋转化为诗。对理解名诗如何从私人情感中诞生有启发。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键启示：最私密、难以言说的恐惧也可能成为创作的材料；理解名诗，也要看到诗背后复杂的人生经验。
articles.sourceExcerpt: This essay is adapted from the nineteenth chapter of my book Figuring. In the first autumn of her thirties, Emily Dickinson wrote to her confidante and eventual editor Thomas Wentworth Higginson: I had a terror — since September — I could tell to none, and so I sing, as the Boy does by the Burying Ground — because I am afraid. Not a “fright,” not a “shock,” but a terror.

en.highlight: I had a terror — since September — I could tell to none, and so I sing, as the Boy does by the Burying Ground — because I am afraid.
en.summary: This essay, adapted from the nineteenth chapter of Figuring, begins with Emily Dickinson’s letter to Thomas Wentworth Higginson about a terror she could tell to none, and explores the emotional story behind her most famous poem, “Hope Is the Thing with Feathers.” Biographers have long filled the gap with conjectures such as a death, while the essay focuses on how private fear and unrequited love were transformed into poetry. It is worth reading for a closer view of how a famous poem can grow out of intimate, difficult experience.
en.failureAnalysis: Key takeaway: the most private and unspeakable terror can become the raw material of art; reading a famous poem means also seeing the complex life behind it.
en.title: Hope Is the Thing with Feathers, and with Fangs: The Alchemy of Unrequited Love and the Story Behind Emily Dickinson’s Most Famous Poem

en.failureAnalysis: The key risk is default data flow and trust, not model capability: if identity details such as email addresses are exposed unintentionally, users may question whether the tool is suitable for private code. Fixing it requires tracing the request path, changing defaults, and communicating clearly, or enterprise security reviews and adoption may be delayed.
en.title: Claude Code Sends Your Email Address to Websites

en.summary: This is a GitHub repository called unigit-ecosystem with about 2,288 stars and recent public activity, describing itself as UNIGIT's public brand and ecosystem hub under the slogan "AI should work for everyone." Only the repository description and popularity signals are visible; no product form, technical implementation, or deployment path is disclosed. It is worth a quick look mainly as a sample of how an AI-for-everyone narrative gets packaged as an ecosystem brand, not as evidence of technical value.
en.failureAnalysis: A repo positioned as a brand and ecosystem hub rather than a product risks being all narrative with no verifiable user value, since the actual users, scenarios, and pain points are undisclosed.
